prompt:
Turn REFERENCE IMAGE 1, a flat schematic floor plan, into ONE finished illustrated
top-down floor plan of the same living room. Keep EXACTLY the layout of image 1:
same room outline, same wall openings, same position, size, shape and orientation
of every piece of furniture. Do not move, rotate, resize, add or remove anything.
Camera strictly vertical above the room (orthographic, ceiling removed): no
perspective, no visible wall faces, walls shown as thick dark outlines from above.

What each shape in image 1 is: blue band in the top wall = large floor-to-ceiling
window with the two grey curtain bundles beside it; dark grey L-shape = dark grey
fabric L-shaped sofa with cushions, its long section parallel to the window and its
return along the left side; small brown square with yellow disc, top-left = side
table with a warm amber table lamp; green circle beside it = large potted plant;
dark rectangle = dark patterned rug; brown rectangle on the rug = rectangular wooden
coffee table with a dark mug, a small bowl, a remote and a few books; long brown
rectangle on the right wall = low wooden TV cabinet; thin black line with green edge
in front of it = flat TV facing the sofa; tall brown rectangle top-right = bookshelf
with books; green circle bottom-right = small potted plant; small black bars on the
left and right walls = two framed pictures hanging on the walls; opening with door
arc, bottom-left = entrance door opening inward; small dark square bottom-left =
coat hook with a dark coat; tan floor = warm wooden parquet. Dashed bottom edge =
plain wall. Add a knitted throw on the sofa's left section.

REFERENCE IMAGE 2 is the same room seen in perspective: use it ONLY for materials,
colours and graphic style (fine visible contours, painterly faceted shading, dark
olive night ambience, warm amber lamp glow, cool green TV glow), never for layout or
camera angle. Keep enough soft light for every object to stay readable.
No people, no animals, no text, labels, numbers, legend, arrows or watermark.
